summary: Orkora is developing offshore nuclear power stations exporting multi-gigawatt power to national grids, according to the founder's personal site. No source names the reactor type, a reactor supplier or a customer. A November 2025 job post describes an Aberdeen site building electrically heated test rigs, and the company sells Kortex, a grid site-screening data product.
oneLiner: Developing offshore nuclear power stations to export multi-gigawatt power to national grids, per its founder's site
thesis: A bet on gigawatt-scale nuclear plants built in specialised facilities and operated at sea, spanning energy, shipbuilding and heavy manufacturing. Evidence so far: Aberdeen test rigs, a grid-siting data product and two US lobbying registrations on offshore nuclear permitting.
stage: Orkora Inc. filed a Form D on 18 August 2026: $10,216,689 of equity sold to 6 investors, first sale 23 July 2026, of which $8,000,022.65 was cash and $2,216,666.68 conversion of convertible securities. It names no investors. UK company Orkora Limited's 1 July 2026 confirmation statement lists three shareholders: Ellison (900,000 shares), Thomas Paul Kirk (45,000) and a Cocoa VC fund (45,000). No announcement of the round was found.

team.name: Stuart Ellison
team.background: CEO and director per the Form D. His site lists engineering roles at Submarine Rescue Service, Oil States, Aker Solutions and NIS, and founding Exnics (flow measurement).

team.name: Aditi Maliwal
team.background: Listed as a director on the Form D filed 18 August 2026. The filing gives no affiliation and no other source ties her to the company.

questions: Which reactor goes in the hull, and who designs and supplies it? The siting model assumes 2 GWe per hull, but no source names the reactor type.
Which regulator licenses a station on the high seas (44 of the siting model's 59 sites) or in a foreign EEZ, and where will you file first?
Has Orkora Limited moved under Orkora Inc., where do the IP and Aberdeen staff sit, and who are the six Form D investors?
How is the $8,000,022.65 of new cash split between the reactor programme and Kortex, and what must the sub 20 kW electrically heated rigs show, by when?
risks: No source names a reactor type, supplier or licensing route. A US government article of 23 July 2026 says no offshore nuclear projects have been approved or proposed.
The scale gap is large: $10,216,689 raised and test rigs described as sub 20 kW thermal, against a siting model assuming 2 GWe per hull. Kortex may also split focus.
Filings name only two people, the CEO and one director. No source opened names a team member with reactor design or nuclear licensing experience.
unverified: Whether director Aditi Maliwal is the Upfront Ventures general partner of that name is not confirmed. No source links Upfront Ventures to Orkora.
The six Form D investors are not identified. Cocoa Ventures lists Orkora on its site, but no source says it took part in the Form D round.
A LinkedIn search result describes a Nathaniel Read as Head of Nuclear Engineering at Orkora. The profile could not be opened, so this is not confirmed.

sources.title: Orkora site (siting model in page source)

announcement.what: NEMO announced Orkora as a new full member on its news page, describing a planned fleet of floating nuclear power stations.
